Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake

What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake

What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake

What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake

What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake

What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. In this video: • What orexin A and orexin B are • How orexin helps keep the brain awake • The connection between orexin and narcolepsy type 1 • What cataplexy is • The 2026 breakthrough in orexin-targeted treatment • Why blocking orexin can help people sleep • Orexin's potential roles in appetite, motivation, reward, stress, and metabolism • Why this peptide system could become increasingly important in medicine One peptide system. The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. “The choice that frees or imprisons us is the choice of love or fear. Love liberates. Fear imprisons “. -- Gary Zukav, Spiritual Teacher and New York Times Bestselling Author. His book, Soul Stories, was also a New York Times bestselling book; and many other books he has written that followed. Gary’s books have sold millions of copies and are published in twenty-four languages. He is a graduate of Harvard University and a former U.S. Army Special Forces (Green Beret) officer with Vietnam service. Gary lives in Oregon. Linda Francis was his spiritual partner for decades. Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake

What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. YOUNGER: The Seat of the Soul with Gary Zukav

“The choice that frees or imprisons us is the choice of love or fear. Love liberates. Fear imprisons “. -- Gary Zukav, Spiritual Teacher and New York Times Bestselling Author. Gary Zukav (born October 17, 1942) is an American spiritual teacher, and the author of four consecutive New York Times Best Sellers. Beginning in 1998, he appeared more than 30 times on The Oprah Winfrey Show to discuss transformation in human consciousness which were concepts he presented in his book, The Seat of the Soul. Gary’s first book, The Dancing Wu Li Masters (1979), won a U.S. National Book Award. It is an overview of the New Physics, and became the winner of The American Book Award for Science. Gary’s book The Seat of the Soul, was celebrated as a #1 New York Times Bestseller for three consecutive years in a row. His book, Soul Stories, was also a New York Times bestselling book; and many other books he has written that followed. Gary’s books have sold millions of copies and are published in twenty-four languages. He is a graduate of Harvard University and a former U.S. Army Special Forces (Green Beret) officer with Vietnam service. Gary lives in Oregon. Linda Francis was his spiritual partner for decades. She passed on in 2022, and Gary has said, “She (Linda) was a model to me and many others.” Dr. Robyn Benson's next YOUNGER podcast episode is an interview with "The Seat of the Soul" New York Times Bestselling Author, Gary Zukav. Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake

What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. In this video: • What orexin A and orexin B are • How orexin helps keep the brain awake • The connection between orexin and narcolepsy type 1 • What cataplexy is • The 2026 breakthrough in orexin-targeted treatment • Why blocking orexin can help people sleep • Orexin's potential roles in appetite, motivation, reward, stress, and metabolism • Why this peptide system could become increasingly important in medicine One peptide system. embedding_text:
The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. This is a perfect example of why the question isn't simply “Do peptides work?” The better question is: Which peptide, for what purpose, and where is the human evidence? 📘 FREE Peptide Guide: PeptideAtoZ.com/free-guide 💬 Join the Peptide A to Z Community: PeptideAtoZ.com/community 🔬 Peptide A to Z Research. YOUNGER: The Seat of the Soul with Gary Zukav

“The choice that frees or imprisons us is the choice of love or fear. Love liberates. Fear imprisons “. -- Gary Zukav, Spiritual Teacher and New York Times Bestselling Author. Gary Zukav (born October 17, 1942) is an American spiritual teacher, and the author of four consecutive New York Times Best Sellers. Beginning in 1998, he appeared more than 30 times on The Oprah Winfrey Show to discuss transformation in human consciousness which were concepts he presented in his book, The Seat of the Soul. Gary’s first book, The Dancing Wu Li Masters (1979), won a U.S. National Book Award. It is an overview of the New Physics, and became the winner of The American Book Award for Science. Gary’s book The Seat of the Soul, was celebrated as a #1 New York Times Bestseller for three consecutive years in a row. His book, Soul Stories, was also a New York Times bestselling book; and many other books he has written that followed. Gary’s books have sold millions of copies and are published in twenty-four languages. He is a graduate of Harvard University and a former U.S. Army Special Forces (Green Beret) officer with Vietnam service. Gary lives in Oregon. Linda Francis was his spiritual partner for decades. She passed on in 2022, and Gary has said, “She (Linda) was a model to me and many others.” Dr. Robyn Benson's next YOUNGER podcast episode is an interview with "The Seat of the Soul" New York Times Bestselling Author, Gary Zukav. Watch, listen and learn from this powerful, timely video…

embedding_text:
Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake

What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. In this video: • What orexin A and orexin B are • How orexin helps keep the brain awake • The connection between orexin and narcolepsy type 1 • What cataplexy is • The 2026 breakthrough in orexin-targeted treatment • Why blocking orexin can help people sleep • Orexin's potential roles in appetite, motivation, reward, stress, and metabolism • Why this peptide system could become increasingly important in medicine One peptide system. Turn it down to help people sleep. Turn it up to help people stay awake. Subscribe to Peptide A to Z for straightforward breakdowns of peptide research, clinical studies, and emerging…

The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake

What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. In this video: • What orexin A and orexin B are • How orexin helps keep the brain awake • The connection between orexin and narcolepsy type 1 • What cataplexy is • The 2026 breakthrough in orexin-targeted treatment • Why blocking orexin can help people sleep • Orexin's potential roles in appetite, motivation, reward, stress, and metabolism • Why this peptide system could become increasingly important in medicine One peptide system. The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. YOUNGER: The Seat of the Soul with Gary Zukav

“The choice that frees or imprisons us is the choice of love or fear. Love liberates. Fear imprisons “. -- Gary Zukav, Spiritual Teacher and New York Times Bestselling Author. Gary Zukav (born October 17, 1942) is an American spiritual teacher, and the author of four consecutive New York Times Best Sellers. Beginning in 1998, he appeared more than 30 times on The Oprah Winfrey Show to discuss transformation in human consciousness which were concepts he presented in his book, The Seat of the Soul. Gary’s first book, The Dancing Wu Li Masters (1979), won a U.S. National Book Award. It is an overview of the New Physics, and became the winner of The American Book Award for Science. Gary’s book The Seat of the Soul, was celebrated as a #1 New York Times Bestseller for three consecutive years in a row. His book, Soul Stories, was also a New York Times bestselling book; and many other books he has written that followed. Gary’s books have sold millions of copies and are published in twenty-four languages. He is a graduate of Harvard University and a former U.S. Army Special Forces (Green Beret) officer with Vietnam service. Gary lives in Oregon. Linda Francis was his spiritual partner for decades. She passed on in 2022, and Gary has said, “She (Linda) was a model to me and many others.” Dr. Robyn Benson's next YOUNGER podcast episode is an interview with "The Seat of the Soul" New York Times Bestselling Author, Gary Zukav. Watch, listen and learn from this powerful, timely video…

Carolina Reis de Oliveira on Reversing Skin Age, Menopause, GLP-1 Skin, and the Science of Senescent Cells For Dave’s listeners only, visit oneskin.co/Dave for exclusive early access to the OS-01 Face Rich Cream! Host Dave Asprey sits down with Carolina Reis de Oliveira, PhD, CEO and co-founder of OneSkin. Carolina holds a PhD in stem cell biology and tissue engineering, is a co-inventor of five patents, and has co-authored numerous scientific publications. She and her team are studying skin longevity by targeting one of the central drivers of aging: the accumulation of senescent cells. They break down why skin loses its ability to hold water as you age, and why that process can accelerate dramatically during perimenopause and menopause. Carolina explains the skin's "brick and mortar" barrier system, how declining estrogen affects collagen, ceramides, cholesterol, hyaluronic acid, and elastin, and why simply sealing moisture into your skin with occlusive products does not solve the underlying biology. They also explore why GLP-1 users can experience loose or sagging skin after rapid weight loss and what may help preserve skin structure over time. Carolina reveals how her team screened hundreds of peptides to develop OS-01, a senomorphic peptide designed to reduce the damaging signals produced by senescent "zombie" cells while supporting healthier skin function. In their research, OS-01 reduced markers of cellular senescence and inflammation, increased collagen production…

Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake

What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. In this video: • What orexin A and orexin B are • How orexin helps keep the brain awake • The connection between orexin and narcolepsy type 1 • What cataplexy is • The 2026 breakthrough in orexin-targeted treatment • Why blocking orexin can help people sleep • Orexin's potential roles in appetite, motivation, reward, stress, and metabolism • Why this peptide system could become increasingly important in medicine One peptide system. The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. “The choice that frees or imprisons us is the choice of love or fear. Love liberates. Fear imprisons “. -- Gary Zukav, Spiritual Teacher and New York Times Bestselling Author. Gary Zukav (born October 17, 1942) is an American spiritual teacher, and the author of four consecutive New York Times Best Sellers. Beginning in 1998, he appeared more than 30 times on The Oprah Winfrey Show to discuss transformation in human consciousness which were concepts he presented in his book, The Seat of the Soul. Gary’s first book, The Dancing Wu Li Masters (1979), won a U.S. National Book Award. It is an overview of the New Physics, and became the winner of The American Book Award for Science. Gary’s book The Seat of the Soul, was celebrated as a #1 New York Times Bestseller for three consecutive years in a row. His book, Soul Stories, was also a New York Times bestselling book; and many other books he has written that followed. Gary’s books have sold millions of copies and are published in twenty-four languages. He is a graduate of Harvard University and a former U.S. Army Special Forces (Green Beret) officer with Vietnam service. Gary lives in Oregon. Linda Francis was his spiritual partner for decades. She passed on in 2022, and Gary has said, “She (Linda) was a model to me and many others.” Dr. Robyn Benson's next YOUNGER podcast episode is an interview with "The Seat of the Soul" New York Times Bestselling Author, Gary Zukav. Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake

What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake

What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. In this video: • What orexin A and orexin B are • How orexin helps keep the brain awake • The connection between orexin and narcolepsy type 1 • What cataplexy is • The 2026 breakthrough in orexin-targeted treatment • Why blocking orexin can help people sleep • Orexin's potential roles in appetite, motivation, reward, stress, and metabolism • Why this peptide system could become increasingly important in medicine One peptide system. Turn it down to help people sleep. Turn it up to help people stay awake. Subscribe to Peptide A to Z for straightforward breakdowns of peptide research, clinical studies, and emerging…

The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. How to Heal Your Cells | Dr. Will Cole

We talk about aging like it happens to a whole person at once. It doesn't. It happens organ by organ, at different speeds, and most people never find out which part of them is running ahead until something breaks. Dr. Will Cole has spent sixteen years running one of the first functional medicine telehealth centers in the world, and he came to this conversation with a case that is both clinical and personal. In 2023 his father lost consciousness at the wheel and died in the crash. The autopsy pointed to cardiometabolic changes, and his heart cells had been aging faster than the rest of him. That same year, Stanford researchers found that one in five adults over fifty has at least one organ aging faster than the others, and that when it's the heart, the risk of a cardiac event more than triples. His new book with Dr. Josh Axe, Heal Your Cells, makes an argument that reframes most of what gets called normal aging. Exhaustion, brain fog, the weight that will not move, the hormone shifts nobody can explain. These are not the calendar. They are cells that have stopped reading their own instructions clearly, and that is a state you can change. We also get…

Your Gut Is Talking to Your Brain: Here’s What It’s Saying

Your gut isn't just digesting food. It's talking to your brain constantly, through the vagus nerve, through neurotransmitters, through inflammation signals that shape mood, focus, and stress response. Your oral microbiome is doing its own signaling too. Research links oral bacteria to cardiovascular health, since certain strains can enter the bloodstream and contribute to arterial inflammation. Gut and oral health are highly individual. What heals one person's gut can quietly feed the wrong bacteria in someone else's. Generic advice like "eat more fiber" or "take a probiotic" often misses the mark because it isn't built around your specific microbiome. Viome tests your gut and oral microbiome directly, then gives you a personalized breakdown of which foods to eat, which to avoid, and which supplements actually match your biology.

Glucagon Explained: The Peptide Behind Retatrutide’s Secret Weapon

What if one of the most important peptides in your body does almost the OPPOSITE of insulin? It's called glucagon. Insulin helps lower blood sugar. Glucagon can help raise it — and it's so powerful that glucagon is used as an emergency medicine for severe low blood sugar. But that's only part of the story. Scientists are now targeting the glucagon system alongside GLP-1 and GIP in retatrutide, an experimental triple-receptor agonist producing remarkable results in human trials. In this video, we break down: What glucagon is and how it works Why glucagon can raise blood sugar How glucagon differs from insulin Why glucagon is an established medicine Why scientists would target glucagon for weight loss How retatrutide targets GLP-1 + GIP + glucagon The human evidence behind retatrutide Why “glucagon is the opposite of insulin” is useful — but an oversimplification In a Phase 2 trial, the highest retatrutide dose produced 24.2% average weight loss at 48 weeks. More recently, Lilly reported 28.3% average weight loss at 80 weeks at the highest dose in its Phase 3 TRIUMPH-1 trial. The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. This is a perfect example of why the question isn't simply “Do peptides work?” The better question is: Which peptide, for what purpose, and where is the human evidence? 📘 FREE Peptide Guide: PeptideAtoZ.com/free-guide 💬 Join the Peptide A to Z Community: PeptideAtoZ.com/community 🔬 Peptide A to Z Research. How to Heal Your Cells | Dr. Will Cole

We talk about aging like it happens to a whole person at once. It doesn't. It happens organ by organ, at different speeds, and most people never find out which part of them is running ahead until something breaks. Dr. Will Cole has spent sixteen years running one of the first functional medicine telehealth centers in the world, and he came to this conversation with a case that is both clinical and personal. In 2023 his father lost consciousness at the wheel and died in the crash. The autopsy pointed to cardiometabolic changes, and his heart cells had been aging faster than the rest of him. That same year, Stanford researchers found that one in five adults over fifty has at least one organ aging faster than the others, and that when it's the heart, the risk of a cardiac event more than triples. His new book with Dr. Josh Axe, Heal Your Cells, makes an argument that reframes most of what gets called normal aging. Exhaustion, brain fog, the weight that will not move, the hormone shifts nobody can explain. These are not the calendar. They are cells that have stopped reading their own instructions clearly, and that is a state you can change. We get into what actually makes a cell feel unsafe, why your gut lining is one cell thick and therefore the first thing to break, and the point almost nobody makes about elimination diets: the reintroduction matters as much as the elimination, and a protocol you never came off of is a cast you left on until the muscle atrophied. The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. embedding_text:
What Sauna Research Actually Shows About Longevity

Sauna is one of the longevity practices I use consistently, but the evidence needs to be described honestly. The widely shared reductions in mortality, cardiovascular events, and dementia come largely from observational Finnish data, not randomized trials proving sauna caused those outcomes. The research is still compelling enough to take seriously, especially around cardiovascular conditioning and heat adaptation, but it is not a guarantee. I also track my own toxic-burden results and have seen lower levels during periods when I use sauna. That is useful personal data, not proof that sauna “detoxes” everyone. My approach is to separate established evidence, promising associations, and personal response. Hydration, heat tolerance, medical conditions, and recovery still matter more than chasing the hottest temperature or longest session. #Sauna #Longevity #HeatTherapy #CardiovascularHealth #HealthyAging

Your Gut Is Talking to Your Brain: Here’s What It’s Saying

Your gut isn't just digesting food. It's talking to your brain constantly, through the vagus nerve, through neurotransmitters, through inflammation signals that shape mood, focus, and stress response. Your oral microbiome is doing its own signaling too. Research links oral bacteria to cardiovascular health, since certain strains can enter the bloodstream and contribute to arterial inflammation. Gut and oral health are highly individual. What heals one person's gut can quietly feed the wrong bacteria in someone else's. Generic advice like "eat more fiber" or "take a probiotic" often misses the mark because it isn't built around your specific microbiome. Viome tests your gut and oral microbiome directly, then gives you a personalized breakdown of which foods to eat, which to avoid, and which supplements actually match your biology.

Glucagon Explained: The Peptide Behind Retatrutide’s Secret Weapon

What if one of the most important peptides in your body does almost the OPPOSITE of insulin? It's called glucagon. Insulin helps lower blood sugar. Glucagon can help raise it — and it's so powerful that glucagon is used as an emergency medicine for severe low blood sugar. But that's only part of the story. Scientists are now targeting the glucagon system alongside GLP-1 and GIP in retatrutide, an experimental triple-receptor agonist producing remarkable results in human trials. In this video, we break down: What glucagon is and how it works Why glucagon can raise blood sugar How glucagon differs from insulin Why glucagon is an established medicine Why scientists would target glucagon for weight loss How retatrutide targets GLP-1 + GIP + glucagon The human evidence behind retatrutide Why “glucagon is the opposite of insulin” is useful — but an oversimplification In a Phase 2 trial, the highest retatrutide dose produced 24.2% average weight loss at 48 weeks. The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. embedding_text:
What Sauna Research Actually Shows About Longevity

Sauna is one of the longevity practices I use consistently, but the evidence needs to be described honestly. The widely shared reductions in mortality, cardiovascular events, and dementia come largely from observational Finnish data, not randomized trials proving sauna caused those outcomes. The research is still compelling enough to take seriously, especially around cardiovascular conditioning and heat adaptation, but it is not a guarantee. I also track my own toxic-burden results and have seen lower levels during periods when I use sauna. That is useful personal data, not proof that sauna “detoxes” everyone. My approach is to separate established evidence, promising associations, and personal response. Hydration, heat tolerance, medical conditions, and recovery still matter more than chasing the hottest temperature or longest session. #Sauna #Longevity #HeatTherapy #CardiovascularHealth #HealthyAging

Launch HN: RonanRX (YC S26) – Personalized Peptides and GLP-1s

Hi HN, I’m Lloyd, one of two founders of RonanRx ( https://ronanrx.com/ ). We are building a vertically integrated pharmaceutical company with software for prescribing, telehealth, compounding, manufacturing, and delivery. We are starting with GLP-1s and peptides. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. embedding_text:
Your Indoor Air May Be Working Against Your Health

Air is one of our largest daily exposures and one of the easiest to ignore because you cannot see most pollutants. I do not think home optimization should begin with buying every gadget. It should begin with measurement. PM2.5, VOCs, humidity, and CO2 can reveal whether cooking, cleaning products, poor ventilation, smoke, or an overcrowded room are changing the air you breathe. Once you know the problem, interventions become more rational: ventilation when outdoor air is clean, source control, appropriate filtration, and regular maintenance. A plant may improve the feel of a room, but it should not replace filtration or ventilation. My approach is to make the environments where I spend the most time as supportive as realistically possible, rather than trying to control every exposure in the world. #IndoorAirQuality #HealthyHome #AirPollution #EnvironmentalHealth #Longevity

embedding_text:
Your Indoor Air May Be Working Against Your Health

Air is one of our largest daily exposures and one of the easiest to ignore because you cannot see most pollutants. I do not think home optimization should begin with buying every gadget. It should begin with measurement. PM2.5, VOCs, humidity, and CO2 can reveal whether cooking, cleaning products, poor ventilation, smoke, or an overcrowded room are changing the air you breathe. Once you know the problem, interventions become more rational: ventilation when outdoor air is clean, source control, appropriate filtration, and regular maintenance. A plant may improve the feel of a room, but it should not replace filtration or ventilation. My approach is to make the environments where I spend the most time as supportive as realistically possible, rather than trying to control every exposure in the world. #IndoorAirQuality #HealthyHome #AirPollution #EnvironmentalHealth #Longevity

embedding_text:
Your Indoor Air May Be Working Against Your Health

Air is one of our largest daily exposures and one of the easiest to ignore because you cannot see most pollutants. I do not think home optimization should begin with buying every gadget. It should begin with measurement. PM2.5, VOCs, humidity, and CO2 can reveal whether cooking, cleaning products, poor ventilation, smoke, or an overcrowded room are changing the air you breathe. Once you know the problem, interventions become more rational: ventilation when outdoor air is clean, source control, appropriate filtration, and regular maintenance. A plant may improve the feel of a room, but it should not replace filtration or ventilation. My approach is to make the environments where I spend the most time as supportive as realistically possible, rather than trying to control every exposure in the world. #IndoorAirQuality #HealthyHome #AirPollution #EnvironmentalHealth #Longevity

embedding_text:
Your Indoor Air May Be Working Against Your Health

Air is one of our largest daily exposures and one of the easiest to ignore because you cannot see most pollutants. I do not think home optimization should begin with buying every gadget. It should begin with measurement. PM2.5, VOCs, humidity, and CO2 can reveal whether cooking, cleaning products, poor ventilation, smoke, or an overcrowded room are changing the air you breathe. Once you know the problem, interventions become more rational: ventilation when outdoor air is clean, source control, appropriate filtration, and regular maintenance. A plant may improve the feel of a room, but it should not replace filtration or ventilation. My approach is to make the environments where I spend the most time as supportive as realistically possible, rather than trying to control every exposure in the world. #IndoorAirQuality #HealthyHome #AirPollution #EnvironmentalHealth #Longevity
